title: Tottenham’s Guglielmo Vicario to be sidelined for up to a month after hernia surgery
content:
Tottenham Hotspur’s first-choice goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario will have an operation on his hernia next week, ruling him out of action for up to a month.

Vicario played the entirety of Wednesday’s 3-2 victory over Atletico in the return leg and will be available for Sunday’s crucial relegation six-pointer against Nottingham Forest.

The Italy international has started all of Spurs’ games in the Premier League this season but he was dropped to the bench for the first leg of their last 16-tie against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League last week. Back-up goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky made errors leading to two Atleti goals in a disastrous start for Spurs, and the young Czech was replaced by Vicario with the hosts leading 3-0 in the 17th minute.

After facing Forest, the 29-year-old will undergo surgery and be unavailable for around a month. Spurs do not have another game for three weeks after they play Forest due to the international break and because they have been knocked out of the FA Cup and the Champions League. Their first fixture after the international break is against Sunderland on April 12, before the host Brighton & Hove Albion on April 18.

“We can confirm that Guglielmo Vicario will undergo surgery next week on a hernia,” Spurs said in a statement released on Friday.

“The minor procedure for the Italy international goalkeeper has been timed to have as minimal impact on our season as possible. Guglielmo will commence his rehabilitation with our medical staff immediately, and it is hoped that he could return to action within the next month.”

It is a huge blow for Spurs as their injury crisis was slowly improving. Destiny Udogie and Lucas Bergvall returned to action against Atletico while interim head coach Igor Tudor revealed in his press conference on Friday that there is hope James Maddison could feature this season.

Just when it looked like Spurs’ fortunes were starting to improve under interim head coach Igor Tudor, they have been rocked by the news that Vicario requires surgery.

It has been a dismal season for Spurs and this is the latest obstacle which has been thrown in their path. Vicario’s form has been erratic but his fantastic save from Giuliano Simeone’s deflected shot in Wednesday’s victory over Atletico Madrid underlined his quality. The 29-year-old is a member of the dressing room’s senior leadership group and his experience will be sorely missed.

The only positive to emerge from this scenario is it offers Kinksy an opportunity to redeem himself after a nightmare performance in Madrid. Kinsky gifted Atletico two goals before Tudor dragged him off the pitch. Kinsky walked straight down the tunnel and it was difficult to imagine him playing for Spurs again anytime soon. Nobody has ever doubted the Czech Republic Under-21 international’s potential but he needs to play regularly to fulfill it.

Before last weekend’s draw with Liverpool, Tudor was asked if he would have any hesitation about playing Kinsky again during the rest of the season.

“No, of course he will play for sure,” Tudor said. “He came back the day after and was very good in training. Positive. Nothing else. So this situation happened, very rare, probably the first and last time in my life and the life of a lot of people but this can happen. It is the same message I said before. You can go out from the situation as a victim. ‘Poor me what happened.’ Everybody sending a message of help and I am with you. This is nice also.

“Sometimes 2025 this social media life became like it is more important what you say than what you do. But as I said before, this is normal, this is a mistake that will happen. For sure in his career there will be other mistakes but he has a strength and quality and in front of him is a very good career.”

The 23-year-old has been given a second chance quicker than anybody expected it and he needs to grasp it.
